clue.text: Burn coats off back in worker's platform

indicators.note: to coat something is to wrap round it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to scald is to burn with hot liquid or steam

indicators.note: putting a word back means reading it from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker gets scalded and has to strip off a coat while standing up on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coats' looks like clothing, but here it is a verb: the burn wraps round the other piece, which is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders and painters stand on this temporary framework of poles and planks to work high up.

clue.text: Second Avenue bar

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
Ave is the usual street-sign abbreviation

explanation.surface: A tavern on New York's Second Avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a drinking place, but it is the preposition meaning except, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions both mean except: 'everyone save John' is everyone apart from John.

clue.text: Nothing is found in craft (a vessel)

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the rest

parts.note: a craft is a skill or art
taken as written
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A boat turns out to be empty: nothing aboard the craft.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside ARTA, just after its first letter. 'Craft' and 'vessel' both suggest boats, but the vessel is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, the largest blood vessel leading from the heart.

clue.text: Direct Howard to enter disorderly flat

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is put within the other
something disorderly is out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Ron Howard is the American actor and film director

explanation.surface: An order to send someone called Howard into a messy apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like a verb opening an instruction; it is the adjective, as in a direct or head-on attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontal attack or challenge is head-on and straightforward, meeting its target directly.

clue.text: Overtake Arizona city

parts.note: to lap a runner is to overtake them by a full circuit
AZ is the US postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: A driver passes the traffic in some Arizona town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arizona city' looks like one phrase asking for Phoenix or Tucson, but the city is in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: La Paz, in the Andes, is the seat of Bolivia's government and one of its largest urban centres.

clue.text: Pertaining to an ancient system of enmity?

definitions.text: Pertaining to an ancient system of enmity?

parts.note: surface reading: relating to the medieval order of lords, vassals and land held in return for service
setter's reading: the word split as a quarrel plus the adjective ending -al, so 'having to do with a long-running quarrel'

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the word for the medieval landholding system can be heard as a long quarrel plus a suffix meaning 'relating to'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the medieval European order in which land was held from a lord in exchange for service.

clue.text: Change ensured for consumer

indicators.note: to change the word is to alter its form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper guarantees that customers get the right change.
explanation.definitionFit: The final buyer or user of a product, as opposed to a retailer or maker, is its consumer.

clue.text: Eerie canal held a Charleston venue, perhaps

indicators.note: something eerie is weird and unnatural, so the letters are turned into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spooky stretch of the Erie Canal hosted something in Charleston, South Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eerie canal' echoes the Erie Canal in New York. Charleston looks like the city, but it is the 1920s dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance, so a public ballroom is a place where it might be danced.

clue.text: Where to find wood and grease applied around dark brown masonry, ultimately

indicators.note: something applied around a thing is spread on all sides of it, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: lard is pig fat, a cooking grease
umber is a dark brown earth pigment

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of that word is used

parts.note: last letter of masonry

explanation.surface: Building instructions: grease smeared over brown stonework, and where to get timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The grease is split open after its first letter so the colour and the final letter sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberyard is a business that stores and sells timber, so it is where one goes to buy wood.

clue.text: Engineer had ample gear for a miner

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct or contrive it, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineer was well equipped with kit for working underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like the person in the scene, but it is a verb telling you to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners wear a lamp strapped to the helmet or forehead to light their work underground.

clue.text: Sign and leave after six runs

indicators.note: after says the following piece is placed behind the ones named next, setting the order of the parts

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
R is the cricket and baseball scoring abbreviation for runs
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A cricketer signs an autograph and leaves after scoring a boundary six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a verb, as in signing a form; it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo, the Virgin, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, covering late August to late September.

clue.text: Does my pun upset Lewis Carroll, for instance?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone worries that a joke would offend the author of Alice in Wonderland, a famous lover of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, so it is an example of an assumed name.

clue.text: Poured water on blemish, with father turning over in bed

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the last word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning over flips the pair end to end, so they are read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
zit is slang for a pimple

explanation.surface: Someone threw water on a spot while dad was tossing and turning in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the blemish and the father are turned round together before going into the bed. The American Z spelling is the one the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is a Christian rite in which water is poured or sprinkled on a person, or they are immersed.

clue.text: Went after last piece of shoe leather

parts.note: to go after someone in court is to sue them

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: final letter of shoe

explanation.surface: A cobbler chased off with the final scrap of shoe leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went after' looks like chasing, but it means took legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with the flesh side rubbed to a soft napped finish, often used for shoes.

clue.text: Edward, to serve well, crowns upwardly mobile ditz

indicators.note: in a down answer, moving upward means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
to ace is to serve an unreturnable ball in tennis
caps are tops or crowns

explanation.surface: Edward, a tennis player, goes up in the world and wins titles, yet is a scatterbrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' reads as social climbing, but in a down answer it reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is slang for a dreamy, absent-minded person who seems out of touch with reality.

clue.text: With nothing left inside, cut out

indicators.note: inside says the first pieces go within the word that follows

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim away
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Hollowed so that nothing is left, the piece was cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' looks like one phrase; the definition is only the last word. O and L go inside PARED.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner released early on parole is out of prison, so out here means freed on licence.

clue.text: Uncovered idea for downfall

indicators.note: in a down answer the top letter is the cover, so uncovering removes the first letter

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden bright idea

explanation.surface: An idea is exposed and ruins its author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' looks like ruin, but it is something falling down from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall can be a heavy fall of rain or snow, and a storm with heavy rain is exactly that.

clue.text: Old money's pathetic, sad charm

indicators.note: something pathetic is in a sorry state, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Inherited wealth has a feeble, melancholy appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old money' reads as old-established wealthy families, but it is a former currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece until the euro replaced it in 2002, and was also an ancient coin.

clue.text: Baseball organization to interpret end of play so soon?

parts.note: the AL is the American League of Major League Baseball
to read a situation is to interpret it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: final letter of play

explanation.surface: A baseball league reviews a game that seems to have ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'already?' is surprise that something has happened before it was expected, sooner than seemed likely.

clue.text: Fanny doesn't finish a drink

indicators.note: a word that does not finish loses its final letter

parts.note: in American usage fanny is the buttocks, as is rump

explanation.surface: Someone called Fanny leaves her drink unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny looks like a woman's name; it is American slang for the backside (a different, ruder word in Britain).
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane or molasses, a common alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Tailless ape, 27, is a monster…

indicators.note: something without a tail has lost its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a chimp, short for chimpanzee, is an ape
27 points to the answer of 27-down, Period of time; era is another word for one

explanation.surface: An ape with no tail, crossed with something else, is a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does not supply 27-down's own letters, only a synonym of that answer: an epoch is also an era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast with a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: Excellent, like a seabird toward sunrise

parts.note: E is a school grade for excellent
as means like, as in 'white as snow'
the tern is a gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: A splendid seabird flies off toward the dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' looks like the definition but supplies one letter; E for excellent is a grade on some US report cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun rises in the east, so something lying or heading in that direction is eastern.

clue.text: …in a tree around mid-January

indicators.note: around means the tree goes about the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree

indicators.note: mid points to the middle letter of the month's name

parts.note: the centre letter of the seven-letter January

explanation.surface: Continuing the monster from 20-across: it lurks up a tree in January.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this to 20-across as a single sentence; 'in' is not a container signal here but the definition, as in 'the in crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is fashionable and widely liked, which is what popular means.

clue.text: Gas? That sounds sadistic

indicators.note: that sounds tells you the answer is heard as the next idea when spoken

parts.note: a sadist is in favour of pain

explanation.surface: A cruel remark on a joke: that's not funny, that's cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' could be a laugh or petrol, but it is the fuel. Said aloud the answer is 'pro-pain', in favour of suffering, which is what a sadist is.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a hydrocarbon fuel gas stored in pressurized tanks for grills and heaters.

clue.text: Groups of players in California streets

parts.note: CA is the US postal abbreviation for California
St is the abbreviation for street, plural Sts

explanation.surface: Street bands or film crews out on the roads of California.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is the set of actors in a play or film, the players who perform the roles.

clue.text: Sheltered individual who is likely to regale you at awkward and tedious length about trivial details of his or her everyday life invested in firm

indicators.note: money invested in a business is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: firm and hard both mean solid

parts.words: individual who is likely to regale you at awkward and tedious length about trivial details of his or her everyday life
parts.note: a tiresome talker who goes on and on about dull matters

explanation.surface: A protected person who drones on about daily trivia has put money into a company.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the clue itself goes on at tedious length, like the person it describes. The American -OR spelling is the one the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbor someone is to give them shelter or refuge, so harbored is a past form meaning sheltered.

clue.text: Play organ reflectively, showing off for the king

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
the letters are put on show, lying in plain sight inside the clue's words

parts.note: letters running across the two words, from the second letter of the first

explanation.surface: An organist plays thoughtfully, performing for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden backwards in 'play organ'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit for or belonging to a monarch is royal, the adjective from a king or queen.

clue.text: Period of time to manage rising hydrogen

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: to cope is to manage
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A spell of time spent dealing with hydrogen rising in a lab.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long era of history or geology, a span marked by notable events.

clue.text: Go crazy with false insolence

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for false, as in T/F on a test
lip is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: Someone loses it when given fake cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' looks like an anagram signal, but there is no anagram: it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip, or flip out, is informal for losing one's temper or composure suddenly.

clue.text: Capital prosecutor is captivated by uninteresting ruminant

indicators.note: someone captivated is held captive, so these pieces are held inside the next word

parts.note: dry writing is dull
Rome is the capital of Italy
a DA, district attorney, is a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A city's prosecutor is somehow charmed by a boring cud-chewing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective or money; it is a capital city, here Italy's. DA, district attorney, is the American prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: The dromedary, the one-humped Arabian camel, chews the cud, regurgitating and rechewing its food.

clue.text: Island with a charge

parts.note: taken as written
a toll is a charge, as for a road or bridge

explanation.surface: An island you pay a fee to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island or reef enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Controlling disfigured giant grabbing man's head

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it in the hands, so one piece is held inside the other
a disfigured thing is put out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

parts.note: first letter of man

explanation.surface: A scarred giant seizes a man by the head and gains control.
explanation.definitionFit: Taming is bringing an animal or person under one's control and making them submissive.

clue.text: In public, he redistributed good stock

indicators.note: redistributed means handed out again in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A financier publicly reshuffles a portfolio of sound shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In public' looks like one phrase; 'In' is only the link, and the fodder is the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip shares are those of large, reliable companies, considered safe and sound investments.
